Summary:
The 2015 MIRI review surveys progress on foundational AI-alignment research areas (logical uncertainty, decision theory, Vingean reflection, error tolerance/corrigibility, value specification).  The text contains explicit reasoning chains linking recognised catastrophic AI-safety risks to theoretical insights, algorithms, formal proofs and (sometimes simulated) demonstrations that motivate concrete safety-relevant interventions.  The extracted knowledge fabric below reconstructs those causal-interventional pathways and inter-connects them through a single top-level risk node.

EXTRACTION CONFIDENCE[83]
The paper is largely programmatic, so some intervention details require light inference.  All instructions were followed: every pathway flows Risk→…→Intervention with no direct Risk↔Intervention links, all nodes are connected, framework names were decomposed, and JSON syntax was double-checked.

Inference strategy justification:
Where the article stopped at “algorithm/paper”, I inferred the most obvious near-term intervention an AI-safety practitioner would adopt (e.g. “incorporate logical-uncertainty solvers into reasoning module”).  Edges that rely on such inference are marked confidence 2.

Extraction completeness:
Seven core problem areas explicitly discussed in the review were traced, giving 44 nodes and 55 edges (≈15 nodes/5000 words).  Each MIRI 2015 result that supports an alignment method appears as Implementation-Mechanism and Validation-Evidence nodes, ensuring white-box transparency.

Key limitations:
• Validation evidence is theoretical/proof-based; empirical maturity therefore remains low.  
• The review bundles some research published in 2016; only 2015-initiated content was included.  
• Further granularity (e.g. splitting IM1/IM2 by paper) could be added as more sources are processed.
